audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Gnar the 2+ items row while whys[6], spikes[3] and breakdown.late all say Kassadin out-scales hard.
audit.why: The chart contradicted its own prose and the mirror audit, which already flipped 2+ items to Kassadin.
audit.corrected: win[6] and phases[6].side flipped to Kassadin, phases[6].rating to 4/10, phases[6].why rewritten. Levels 1-5 left with Gnar and Level 6 left Skill — those match the packet chart, the 52.98% win rate and the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: Late-game spike talked about 'stacking Riftwalk charges' with no cooldown number.
audit.why: Riftwalk's rank cooldown is 5/3.5/2 — the rank-3 2-second blink is the actual spike, and it is what beats a 10s-at-rank-5 Boomerang.
audit.corrected: Rank-3 Riftwalk's 2s cooldown added to spikes[3].text, whys[6], late and phases[6].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields claimed Null Sphere silences (whys[2], whys[6], spikes[3].text, early, late). Riot's text gives Null Sphere damage, a channel interrupt and a magic-absorbing shield — no silence. The same fields told the reader Kassadin's shield eats Gnar's poke.
audit.why: Kassadin's Q shield absorbs magic damage; Gnar's Boomerang and autos are physical, so the shield never blocks the poke it was credited with blocking. Two real interactions were absent: Null Sphere is a channel, so Wallop (W) and GNAR! (R) cancel it outright, and Nether Blade is an auto-attack reset — the burst tell is the auto wind-up, not a cast. Void Stone's unit-collision immunity means minions never body-block him.
audit.corrected: Silence removed everywhere; shield stated as magic-only; channel-cancel and Nether Blade auto-reset tell added to early; Void Stone collision-ignore added to late.
sources: enemyKit Null Sphere/Nether Blade/Void Stone text

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Kassadin carry threat 9.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items in, Kassadin takes over: rank-3 Riftwalk blinks every 2s. Carry threat 9.5/10 — close before the map decides for you.

edits.before: He stays meleed-down — kite with the Boomerang slow and Hyper's move speed, and his short-range Q silence can't save him at this distance.
edits.after: He stays meleed-down — kite with the Boomerang slow and Hyper's move speed, and Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic only, so your poke sticks.

edits.before: He out-scales hard: a two-item Kassadin Q-silences your cast and Riftwalk blink-bursts through your kiting, so let your team handle him.
edits.after: He out-scales hard: a two-item Kassadin Riftwalks every 2s at rank 3 and blink-bursts through your kiting, so let your team handle him.

edits.before: Post-Catalyst/Rod-of-Ages Kassadin out-scales: Q silences your Boomerang mid-cast and stacking Riftwalk blink-bursts you faster than you can kite.
edits.after: Post-Catalyst/Rod-of-Ages Kassadin out-scales: rank-3 Riftwalk is a 2s blink, so stacked charges burst you faster than a 10s Boomerang can kite.

edits.before: Kassadin is a sitting duck levels 1-3 — no Riftwalk to escape and a melee range that can't answer your Mini autos or Boomerang. Lead with the Boomerang to slow, walk up and weave autos, and land Hyper's third consecutive hit for the bonus magic damage and a move-speed burst to disengage or stick. His Q shields one packet of your poke and silences your next cast, so bait it with a single auto, then commit the real trade once it's down. Just don't dump your whole Rage bar shoving the wave — you want to enter the all-in in Mega form, not waste the transform on minions.
edits.after: Kassadin is a sitting duck levels 1-3 — no Riftwalk to escape and a melee range that can't answer your Mini autos or Boomerang. Lead with the Boomerang to slow, walk up and weave autos, and land Hyper's third consecutive hit for the bonus magic damage and a move-speed burst to disengage or stick. Null Sphere shields magic only, so it absorbs none of your physical poke, and it is a cast he cannot finish through a Wallop stun. His burst tell is the Nether Blade auto wind-up, not a spell cast — step back on the wind-up. Don't dump your Rage bar shoving the wave: you want to enter the all-in already in Mega form.

edits.before: This is where the lane slips away. A two-item Kassadin with Catalyst/Rod of Ages and stacking Riftwalk charges blink-bursts you, silences your Boomerang the instant you wind it up, and his passive magic shield eats the poke you do land — your front-to-back kiting just can't pin an untargetable blinker. Don't try to solo him after items; cash your early lead into turret plates and objectives, then group. Your wall-ult is still elite teamfight engage, so make the game about catching him out 5v5, not dueling him sidelane.
edits.after: This is where the lane slips away. A two-item Kassadin with Catalyst/Rod of Ages blinks every 2 seconds on rank-3 Riftwalk, and Void Stone both cuts your magic chip and ignores unit collision, so minions never body-block him — your kiting cannot pin a man with a 2-second escape. Don't try to solo him after items; cash your early lead into turret plates and objectives, then group. Your wall-ult is still elite teamfight engage, so make the game about catching him out 5v5, not dueling him sidelane.

notes: Null Sphere was described as a silence in four separate fields; Riot's text gives it damage, a channel interrupt and a magic-absorbing shield. The shield-vs-physical mismatch (Gnar's poke is physical) was also stated as if the shield stopped it. Level chart's 2+ items row flipped to Kassadin to agree with its own prose and the mirror audit; the flip is proposed as one group (win[6], phases[6].side, phases[6].rating, phases[6].why).
